target.pattern: \bswim(?:s|ming)? against the tide\b|\bswam against the tide\b|\bswum against the tide\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Choosing fresh food can feel like swimming against the tide.

brief.meaningEn: Act in opposition to a strong prevailing trend or shared practice.
brief.meaningZh: 逆着強大的主流趨勢或普遍做法行事。
brief.grammar: swim against the tide; swam/swum; often feel like swimming against the tide; specify the prevailing trend.
brief.register: Established water metaphor for opposition to a trend. It does not by itself prove the minority choice is better or doomed.
brief.boundaryZh: 需交代主流及阻力，不只是兩個人不同意；逆流也不代表一定失敗或特別高尚。
brief.misconceptionZh: 分清選擇與趨勢不同，以及選擇有沒有理由或可行支援。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述具體阻力，提出處理方法而非浪漫化少數選擇。

options.en: The proposed cup system ran against the stallholders’ usual practice.
options.zh: 所提杯具安排與攤主慣常做法相反。

options.en: Most stallholders had already stopped using disposable cups.
options.zh: 大部分攤主早已停用即棄杯。

options.en: The collection system was complete before any alternative was discussed.
options.zh: 討論替代方案前，回收安排已完成。

options.en: The proposal simply followed the existing cup arrangement.
options.zh: 提案只是沿用已有杯具安排。

listening.explanationZh: 多數慣用即棄杯與改用可退還杯形成方向對照；仍需處理實際安排。
listening.en: At our street festival, asking stallholders to use the shared returnable cups felt like swimming against the tide: most were used to disposable cups, and we still needed a simple collection system.
listening.zh: 街頭節慶中，請攤主用共用可退還杯，感覺像逆流而行：大部分慣用即棄杯，而我們仍需簡單回收安排。

reply.promptEn: Why did introducing the returnable cups feel difficult?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼引入可退還杯令你覺得有阻力？

options.en: The stalls were used to a different way of serving drinks.
options.zh: 攤位慣用另一種供飲品方法。

options.en: We were swimming against the tide of disposable-cup use and still had to organise collection.
options.zh: 我們逆着用即棄杯的趨勢而行，還需安排回收。

options.en: The change challenged the familiar routine rather than continuing it.
options.zh: 改變挑戰熟悉日程，不是延續它。

options.en: We needed to make an unfamiliar system workable for people following the usual practice.
options.zh: 我們需讓不熟悉的安排，對沿用慣常做法的人可行。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以既有做法及安排需要解釋阻力，不把困難當失敗定論。

scene.promptZh: 小組習慣只用大聲宣傳吸引觀眾，你想試安靜的小型作品交流，需要先解釋做法及試行。哪句貼切？

options.en: We are swimming against the tide of the group’s usual promotional style.
options.zh: 我們正逆着小組慣常宣傳風格而行。

options.en: We are continuing the same loud promotional approach without changes.
options.zh: 我們沒改動，沿用同樣大聲宣傳。

options.en: The group already chose the quiet format before we suggested it.
options.zh: 我們提議前，小組早已選安靜形式。

scene.explanationZh: 與已知慣常方式不同，才有逆主流的對照。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以單靠 swimming against the tide 判斷？

options.en: A person or group is acting against a prevailing trend.
options.zh: 某人或小組逆着主流趨勢行事。

options.en: Their alternative has already been shown to be the best option.
options.zh: 替代方案早已獲證明是最佳。

options.en: The context should identify the trend being resisted.
options.zh: 情境應指出逆着哪個趨勢。

contrast.explanationZh: 與多數不同，不等於方案質素已獲證明。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友認為既是逆流，回收杯方案便不用測試；你還不知道攤主怎收杯。哪句最好？

options.en: Swimming against the tide does not replace a workable collection plan; let us test one with a stall first.
options.zh: 逆流不取代可行收杯安排；先與一個攤位測試吧。

options.en: The unusual idea itself is enough evidence that collection will work.
options.zh: 構思本身少見，就足以證明回收可行。

options.en: Let us return to disposable cups now rather than test a collection point with one stall.
options.zh: 我們現在改回即棄杯，不與一個攤位測收杯點。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先試收杯點才能處理實際操作；少見不等於可行，也不必未測就放棄替代安排。

speaking.en: We were swimming against the tide, so we needed to explain the alternative and test how it would work.
speaking.zh: 我們逆着主流而行，所以需解釋替代方法，並測試怎運作。
speaking.promptZh: 你想說清趨勢及實際下一步。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：戲劇班普遍喜歡快速對白，你寫一幕留長停頓的重逢，想讓未說出口的情感有空間。你知道風格與班上習慣不同，打算試兩種節奏聽回應。用一至兩句英文說明。

examples.en: Writing the reunion with long pauses feels like swimming against the tide in our fast-dialogue class. I want to try both rhythms and hear what the silence adds.
examples.zh: 在偏愛快對白的班上，寫長停頓重逢感覺像逆流；我想試兩種節奏，聽沉默增加甚麼。

examples.en: I am swimming against the tide by leaving space for what the characters cannot say, rather than filling the scene with rapid lines. A rehearsal will help me compare the effect.
examples.zh: 我留空間給角色說不出的事，不以快對白填滿場面，正逆流而行；排練可幫我比較效果。

writing.selfCheckZh: 先指出班上風格，再說停頓的創作目的及試排比較；不把少數風格直接當較好。

takeaways.en: The small press was swimming against the tide by publishing long essays in a market focused on short updates.
takeaways.zh: 市場集中短更新時，小出版社出版長文，是逆流而行。

takeaways.en: She felt she was swimming against the tide when she asked the group to test a slower format.
takeaways.zh: 她請小組試較慢形式時，感到像逆流而行。

lessons.titleZh: 帶出原本不明顯的特質

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A good coach can bring out confidence in quiet players.

brief.meaningEn: Make a quality or feature more noticeable or allow it to develop and be expressed.
brief.meaningZh: 使某項特質或特徵更明顯，或讓它發展及表現出來。
brief.grammar: bring out + quality/feature; bring it out; brought/bringing. A pronoun comes between bring and out.
brief.register: General quality-revealing phrasal verb. The fixed bring out the best in someone is a related, narrower frame; bring out does not always mean the strongest possible performance.
brief.boundaryZh: 需交代帶出哪種特質及依據，不自動表示所有能力提高或只限正面特質。
brief.misconceptionZh: 帶出特質與憑空創造、替人完成作品不同。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明安排或呈現如何令某特點較明顯。

listening.promptZh: 帶出了甚麼，沒有聲稱甚麼？

options.en: Her humour became more visible in that setting, without a claim that her whole personality changed.
options.zh: 該環境令幽默感較明顯，沒說整個性格改了。

options.en: She became the loudest speaker throughout the full meeting.
options.zh: 她在整個大組會議都成為最大聲者。

options.en: The others supplied every humorous line while she only repeated them.
options.zh: 所有幽默對白都由別人提供，她只覆述。

options.en: The rehearsal concealed the humorous details she had already added.
options.zh: 排練掩蓋了她已加的幽默細節。

listening.explanationZh: 實際增添細節顯出幽默，仍拘謹保留不同場合的表現。
listening.en: The small-group rehearsal brought out her quiet humour: with time to try a line, she added details that made the others smile, though she remained reserved in the full meeting.
listening.zh: 小組排練帶出她安靜的幽默感：有時間試一句對白，她加了令大家微笑的細節；大組會議中仍較拘謹。

reply.promptEn: What did the small-group rehearsal reveal about her?
reply.promptZh: 小組排練讓你看見她甚麼特質？

options.en: She had a quiet sense of humour that appeared in the details she tried.
options.zh: 她試的細節顯示安靜的幽默感。

options.en: It brought out her humour by giving her time to try a line.
options.zh: 它給她試對白的時間，帶出幽默感。

options.en: Her playful additions became easier to notice in the smaller setting.
options.zh: 較小環境中，她俏皮的補充較易被留意。

options.en: We saw a side of her performance that the full meeting did not show as clearly.
options.zh: 我們看見大組會議中較不明顯的一面表現。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出環境帶出特質，不改成別人代寫或全面變外向。

scene.promptZh: 你把畫作移到柔和側光下，紋理較清楚，但沒有改畫本身。哪句準確？

options.en: The side light brought out the texture without changing the painting.
options.zh: 側光帶出紋理，沒有改畫作。

options.en: The artist added new texture before the light was moved.
options.zh: 移光前，畫家已加新紋理。

options.en: The texture became less visible in the adjusted light.
options.zh: 調光後，紋理更難看見。

scene.explanationZh: 只是移光令既有紋理較明顯，題目說畫本身未改；不是加筆觸或更難看。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 bring out a quality 的意思？

options.en: A setting allows a previously less visible quality to be expressed.
options.zh: 環境讓原先較不明顯的特質表現出來。

options.en: The feature is hidden so that observers notice it less.
options.zh: 特徵被遮住，令觀察者更少留意。

options.en: A presentation makes an existing detail stand out.
options.zh: 呈現方式令已有細節突出。

contrast.explanationZh: 隱藏與帶出特徵方向不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴以為帶出幽默，就表示人物從此每場合都外向；大組時她仍拘謹。哪句最好？

options.en: The rehearsal brought out her humour in that setting; it did not show a change in every situation.
options.zh: 排練在那環境帶出幽默，不代表每個場合都改了。

options.en: The rehearsal shows that she now leads the full meeting as confidently as the small group.
options.zh: 排練顯示她現在在大組會議，也像小組般有信心帶領。

options.en: Then the humorous details should be ignored because she was not loud later.
options.zh: 那麼因她後來不大聲，幽默細節就應忽略。

dialogue.explanationZh: 大組時仍拘謹，不能由小組幽默推成每場合都自信帶領，也不因後來安靜抹去已見幽默。

speaking.en: The arrangement brought out a quality that had been less visible, without changing the whole person.
speaking.zh: 安排帶出原本較不明顯的特質，卻沒有改變整個人。
speaking.promptZh: 你想說明特質表現的範圍。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你編祖父年輕時的照片展，把相鄰兩張工作照並列，讓觀眾留意他替同事準備工具的小動作；你要說呈現帶出照顧他人的一面，不說照片證明全部人生。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: Placing the two photographs together brings out the care he took in preparing tools for his colleagues. The small action is easier to notice when the images can be compared.
examples.zh: 並列兩張照片，帶出他為同事準備工具的用心；圖片可比較時，小動作較易被留意。

examples.en: The display brings out a considerate side of him through a specific shared-work moment. We should explain that moment rather than claim the photographs tell his whole life.
examples.zh: 展覽透過一個具體合作時刻，帶出他體貼的一面；我們應解釋那一刻，不聲稱照片說盡人生。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把圖片並列與可見小動作連起，描述用心的一面；不憑有限圖像把整個人生定型。

takeaways.en: The slower reading brought out the hesitation in her final sentence.
takeaways.zh: 較慢朗讀帶出她最後一句的猶豫。

takeaways.en: Their questions brought out a thoughtful side of the conversation that I had not noticed before.
takeaways.zh: 他們提問帶出對話中用心思考的一面，是我以往沒留意的。

lessons.titleZh: 圍繞它的一整套生活習慣

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The meal itself matters, but so does the lifestyle wrapped around it.

brief.meaningEn: The surrounding habits and arrangements that give an activity its place in daily life.
brief.meaningZh: 圍繞某活動的習慣及安排，令它在日常生活中形成一套模式。
brief.grammar: the lifestyle wrapped around it; it must refer clearly to the activity already mentioned; wrapped around is a figurative modifier.
brief.register: Creative surrounding-layer metaphor, not a fixed lifestyle diagnosis. It describes a context wider than the activity alone.
brief.boundaryZh: 不能把it留作不明指代，也不憑意象就說每項習慣好或壞。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要指出時間、相處方式或其他日常安排，不只改說活動本身。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體周邊習慣，解釋同一活動為何有不同經驗。

listening.promptZh: it 及周邊層面是甚麼？

options.en: Evening reading, together with the habits and time arranged around it.
options.zh: 晚間閱讀，以及圍繞它安排的習慣及時間。

options.en: A later conversation that replaced the reading rather than followed it.
options.zh: 後來對話取代閱讀，不是在閱讀之後。

options.en: Only the plot, without any reference to the readers’ routine.
options.zh: 只有情節，沒涉及讀者日程。

options.en: A tea-making routine that had replaced reading altogether.
options.zh: 泡茶日程已完全取代閱讀。

listening.explanationZh: reading是it的指代；關訊息、泡茶及讀後交談是周邊日程，沒有說對話取代閱讀或只關情節。
listening.en: Our evening reading was not only about the book; the lifestyle wrapped around it included switching off work messages, making tea and leaving time to talk afterwards.
listening.zh: 我們晚間閱讀不只是書本；圍繞它的生活習慣，包括關掉工作訊息、泡茶及留時間之後交談。

reply.promptEn: Why did the evening reading feel different from reading a few lines during work?
reply.promptZh: 晚間閱讀為甚麼與工作中讀幾行不同？

options.en: We made time without work messages and could talk afterwards.
options.zh: 我們留不受工作訊息打擾的時間，之後也可交談。

options.en: The lifestyle wrapped around it gave the reading time a different place in our day.
options.zh: 圍繞它的生活習慣，令閱讀在日程中有不同位置。

options.en: The surrounding routine mattered alongside the book itself.
options.zh: 除了書本本身，周邊日程也重要。

options.en: Tea, uninterrupted time and later conversation shaped the experience.
options.zh: 茶、不被打斷的時間及之後對話，塑造了體驗。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都提出活動外的安排，不把差異只歸書本內容。

scene.promptZh: 同樣是畫畫，一人與家人晚飯後一起準備材料、畫後分享，另一人趕在通勤空檔畫幾筆；你要說周邊習慣不同。哪句貼切？

options.en: The painting matters, but so does the lifestyle wrapped around it.
options.zh: 畫畫重要，圍繞它的生活習慣也重要。

options.en: The difference concerns only the brand of paint, not the routine.
options.zh: 差異只關油彩品牌，不關日程。

options.en: Both descriptions give exactly the same pattern of time and company.
options.zh: 兩個描述的時間及陪伴模式完全相同。

scene.explanationZh: 相同活動由不同時間及相處安排包圍，經驗不只在材料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜把 the lifestyle wrapped around it 解作？

options.en: The habits surrounding an already identified activity.
options.zh: 圍繞已指明活動的習慣。

options.en: The literal packaging enclosing an object.
options.zh: 實際包住物件的包裝。

options.en: The arrangements that shape how an activity fits into daily life.
options.zh: 塑造活動怎融入日常的安排。

contrast.explanationZh: wrapped 是周邊模式意象，不是包裝紙。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴只寫讀哪本書，卻略去你已說的關訊息及讀後聊天；你想說明晚間閱讀經驗。哪句最好？

options.en: Keep the book, but include the lifestyle wrapped around it, such as our uninterrupted time and later conversation.
options.zh: 保留書本，也加入圍繞它的生活習慣，如不受打斷的時間及之後交談。

options.en: The passage concerns only the book’s subject matter, not the readers’ habits.
options.zh: 段落只關書本內容，不關讀者習慣。

options.en: Then the choice of book alone must explain why the two reading occasions felt different.
options.zh: 那麼單靠選書，一定已解釋兩次閱讀感覺不同。

dialogue.explanationZh: 周邊習慣包括關訊息、讀後聊天；不只書本內容，也不由選書本身獨力解釋全部差異。

speaking.en: The activity mattered, but the lifestyle wrapped around it shaped how it fitted into our day.
speaking.zh: 活動本身重要，圍繞它的生活習慣，也塑造它怎融入日程。
speaking.promptZh: 你想先交代it的指代，再說周邊安排。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫小說人物恢復每周合唱，不只列唱過的歌，也描寫她提早下班、與同伴同行、練後步行回家聊天的安排。用一至兩句英文說明唱歌周邊生活怎改變一周，不把所有改變都歸某首歌。

examples.en: Singing mattered to her, but the lifestyle wrapped around it also changed her week: she left work early and walked home talking with the others. The routine gave the rehearsal a place beyond the songs.
examples.zh: 唱歌對她重要，但圍繞它的生活習慣也改變一周：她提早下班，與同伴邊走回家邊談；日程讓排練不只停在歌曲。

examples.en: Weekly singing became part of her social life: the lifestyle wrapped around it included travelling with the group and talking afterwards. The songs were only one part of that renewed routine.
examples.zh: 每周合唱成為她社交的一部分：圍繞它的生活習慣，包括同行及練後交談；歌曲只是重新建立日程的一部分。

writing.selfCheckZh: 清楚以唱歌或合唱作it指代，再寫工時、同行及練後交流；不把活動周邊安排誤作歌曲內容或包裝。

takeaways.en: The family garden mattered, and the lifestyle wrapped around it included shared mornings and regular conversations with neighbours.
takeaways.zh: 家庭花園重要，圍繞它的生活習慣還包括共度早上及定期與鄰居交談。

takeaways.en: Her painting was shaped by the lifestyle wrapped around it, including the quiet hour she protected after work.
takeaways.zh: 她的畫畫受周邊生活習慣塑造，包括她下班後特意保留的安靜一小時。

lessons.titleZh: 未明文寫下的默契規矩

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Every household has unwritten rules about meals.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Every household has unwritten rules about meals.

brief.meaningEn: Informal expectations people in a group understand, although they are not formally written down.
brief.meaningZh: 群體中大家理解、卻未正式寫下的行為期待。
brief.grammar: an unwritten rule; unwritten rules about + activity; an expectation can be explained aloud and still be unwritten.
brief.register: Conventional social phrase. A shared expectation is not automatically universal, fair or obvious to a newcomer.
brief.boundaryZh: 需說明是哪個群體的期待，不把本地默契推成所有人的規矩。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不熟悉未明文規矩，不一定等於故意失禮；可先說清並協調。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出默契及新成員可能需要的解釋。

options.en: It was an informal local expectation that newcomers might not know.
options.zh: 它是本地非正式期待，新人可能不知道。

options.en: It was printed clearly on the noticeboard for each newcomer.
options.zh: 它清楚印在告示板，供每位新人看。

options.en: It applied only to visitors who had never used the tools.
options.zh: 它只適用從未用工具的訪客。

options.en: The group had decided that nobody should check the bench afterwards.
options.zh: 小組已決定用後不應有人檢查工作台。

listening.explanationZh: 未寫告示仍有群體期待；新人可能需解釋，而不是自動知道。
listening.en: At our workshop, there was an unwritten rule that the last person using the tools checked the bench for the next group; newcomers often needed someone to explain it because it was not on the noticeboard.
listening.zh: 我們工房有條未明文規矩：最後用工具的人替下一組檢查工作台。告示板沒寫，新人常需有人解釋。

reply.promptEn: Why did newcomers sometimes need an explanation about the bench?
reply.promptZh: 新人為甚麼有時需人解釋工作台安排？

options.en: The group expected a check, but the noticeboard did not say so.
options.zh: 小組期待檢查，但告示板沒寫。

options.en: It was an unwritten rule that regular users knew but newcomers might miss.
options.zh: 這是熟客知道、新人卻可能漏知的未明文規矩。

options.en: The expectation was shared informally rather than included in the displayed instructions.
options.zh: 期待非正式傳開，沒列在展示指示。

options.en: Someone needed to make the local practice clear instead of assuming prior knowledge.
options.zh: 應有人說清本地做法，不假定對方已有知識。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出知識落差及需說明，不把新人當故意違規。

scene.promptZh: 劇團習慣所有人試完一段後才給評語，卻沒寫在新人資料；新人中途提建議。哪個描述準確？

options.en: The group had an unwritten rule that had not yet been explained to the newcomer.
options.zh: 小組有未明文規矩，尚未向新人解釋。

options.en: The newcomer had read and agreed to a written rule before interrupting.
options.zh: 新人打斷前，已讀並同意明文規則。

options.en: The group had no expectation about when feedback should be offered.
options.zh: 小組對何時提回饋，沒有期待。

scene.explanationZh: 已有默契與新人不知可並存，沒證據說讀過明文。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 an unwritten rule 推斷？

options.en: A group shares an informal expectation.
options.zh: 群體有共同非正式期待。

options.en: An outsider necessarily knows the expectation before anyone explains it.
options.zh: 外人未獲解釋前，必定已知道期待。

options.en: The practice may need to be explained to new participants.
options.zh: 可能需向新參加者解釋做法。

contrast.explanationZh: 未明文期待不能假定人人預先知道。

dialogue.promptZh: 新人沒做工作台檢查，朋友立刻說他故意不尊重；告示沒寫，也沒人教過。哪句較好？

options.en: Let us explain the unwritten rule before judging why he missed it.
options.zh: 我們先解釋未明文規矩，再判斷他為何漏做。

options.en: He arrived at the workshop, so he already knew the local bench routine.
options.zh: 他既到工房，就早已知道本地工作台日程。

options.en: Then the regular users’ expectation cannot exist because it was not printed.
options.zh: 那麼沒印出來，熟客的期待就不可能存在。

dialogue.explanationZh: 到場不證明知道未解釋的本地期待；先解釋做法，不能推故意，也不因未印便否定期待存在。

speaking.en: The unwritten rule was familiar to regular members, but new participants still needed a clear explanation.
speaking.zh: 熟客熟悉未明文規矩，新參加者仍需清楚解釋。
speaking.promptZh: 你想交代群體默契與新人理解。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寄住親戚家，發現大家飯後先把碗放固定位置，再一起收桌，卻沒人說這安排；你想禮貌問清楚，不假定自家做法必適合。用一至兩句英文說明。

examples.en: There seems to be an unwritten rule about where the bowls go after dinner. Could you show me the usual arrangement so I can help?
examples.zh: 飯後碗放哪裏，似有未明文規矩。你可示範慣常安排，讓我幫忙嗎？

examples.en: I may have missed an unwritten rule in this household, so I would rather ask about clearing the table than assume my own routine fits.
examples.zh: 我可能漏知這家庭的未明文規矩，所以寧願問怎收桌，不假定自家日程適用。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以初到別家主動問習慣，處理未知默契；不把觀察當所有家庭同一規矩，或直接指責主人沒寫。

takeaways.en: The new players asked about the unwritten rules of the rehearsal before offering feedback.
takeaways.zh: 新隊員提回饋前，先問排練的未明文規矩。

takeaways.en: An unwritten rule about using the shared shelf became easier to follow once someone explained its purpose.
takeaways.zh: 有人解釋用途後，共用架子的未明文規矩較易跟從。

sources.sentence: A courteous greeting can send clear signals of respect.

brief.meaningEn: Communicate an attitude, intention or message clearly through words or actions.
brief.meaningZh: 透過說話或行動，清楚傳達態度、意圖或意思。
brief.grammar: send a clear signal that + clause; send clear signals of + attitude; sent/sending.
brief.register: Natural signalling collocation, often figurative when behaviour conveys an attitude. A signal of attention is not necessarily agreement.
brief.boundaryZh: 訊號要按具體場合理解；說清發出甚麼意思，不假定收訊者所有理解都一樣。
brief.misconceptionZh: 外在動作可提供線索，但不自動證明未說的承諾或私下想法。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述行動傳達的有限意思，並在不確定時核對。

listening.promptZh: 行動傳達甚麼，沒傳達甚麼？

options.en: Willingness to listen, not prior agreement with the proposal.
options.zh: 願意聆聽，不是事先同意提案。

options.en: Approval of the final proposal before it was explained.
options.zh: 提案未解釋前，已批准最後方案。

options.en: A wish to end the conversation without hearing the speaker.
options.zh: 不聽說話者，想結束對話。

options.en: A promise to put the proposal into practice without questions.
options.zh: 承諾不提問題便實行提案。

listening.explanationZh: 動作對應準備聽，未聽提案不能改成已同意或承諾。
listening.en: By putting my phone away and turning towards the speaker, I sent clear signals that I was ready to listen; I had not yet agreed with the proposal she was about to explain.
listening.zh: 我收起電話、轉向說話者，發出清楚訊號表示準備聆聽；她還未解釋提案，我並未同意。

reply.promptEn: What did putting the phone away communicate before the discussion?
reply.promptZh: 討論前收起電話，傳達了甚麼？

options.en: I was giving the speaker my attention.
options.zh: 我把注意力給說話者。

options.en: It sent clear signals that I was ready to listen, not that I had already agreed.
options.zh: 它發出清楚訊號，表示準備聽，不是已同意。

options.en: The action showed I wanted to hear the explanation before responding.
options.zh: 行動顯示我想先聽解釋再回應。

options.en: I was making space for the conversation without settling my view of the proposal.
options.zh: 我為對話留空間，尚未定對提案的看法。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都保留注意與同意的界線。

scene.promptZh: 活動現場已滿，你掛上「本場額滿」並指向下一場登記處，想讓新到者明白今場不能再入、可查下一場，而非已有下一場座位。哪句準確？

options.en: The notices send clear signals that this session is full and visitors should ask about the next one.
options.zh: 告示清楚傳達本場已滿，訪客應查詢下一場。

options.en: The notices confirm that every new arrival already has a reserved place in the next session.
options.zh: 告示確認每位新到者已有下一場預留座位。

options.en: The notices invite more people into the current session because seats are still available.
options.zh: 告示邀更多人入今場，因仍有座位。

scene.explanationZh: 告示傳達今場容量及下一步查詢，不保證下一場已預留，也不是今場仍有空。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 a clear signal of attention 得出？

options.en: The person is communicating readiness to listen.
options.zh: 當事人在傳達準備聆聽。

options.en: The person has accepted the other side’s proposed decision.
options.zh: 當事人已接受對方所提決定。

options.en: Context identifies which action communicates the message.
options.zh: 情境指出哪個行動傳達意思。

contrast.explanationZh: 注意不等於決定同意。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把你收電話的動作寫成已答應提案，但你只是想先聽。哪句回應最好？

options.en: I sent clear signals that I would listen; I still needed to hear the proposal before deciding.
options.zh: 我清楚表示會聽；決定前仍需聽提案。

options.en: Yes, putting the phone away meant I had already approved the proposal before hearing it.
options.zh: 對，收電話表示我未聽提案前已批准。

options.en: I had already settled my response before hearing her explanation.
options.zh: 我未聽她解釋，早已定好回應。

dialogue.explanationZh: 收電話表示準備聆聽；不能答成已批准，也不能推早已定好回應。

speaking.en: My actions sent clear signals that I was paying attention, while the decision still needed discussion.
speaking.zh: 我的行動清楚傳達正在留意，而決定仍需討論。
speaking.promptZh: 你想交代訊號內容及未決部分。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為小組共用草稿設標示，把未核對段落標作「待核」，另列檢查人名及日期，想讓合作者知道可以看、卻還未適合公開。用一至兩句英文說明這套安排傳達的意思。

examples.en: The pending-review label and checklist send clear signals that the draft is open to the group but not ready to publish. We should explain what still needs checking before sharing it more widely.
examples.zh: 待核標示與檢查清單，清楚傳達草稿可供小組看，但未能公開；更廣分享前，應說明仍需核甚麼。

examples.en: We can send a clear signal about the draft’s status by separating the review copy from the approved version. Contributors can then add comments without treating it as final.
examples.zh: 我們把審閱本與批准版本分開，可清楚傳達草稿狀態；合作者便可加評語，不當定稿。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以版本及待核標示傳達可閱但未定稿的狀態；仍需合作者明白標示，不能只上色便假定人人看懂。

takeaways.en: Leaving a named contact sent clear signals that questions were welcome before the deadline.
takeaways.zh: 列出指定聯絡人，清楚傳達期限前歡迎提問。

takeaways.en: The separate draft folder sent a clear signal that those files were still being reviewed.
takeaways.zh: 獨立草稿夾清楚傳達，那些檔案仍在審閱。

lessons.titleZh: 傳達人際價值的社交語言

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Table manners act as a social language at family meals.

brief.meaningEn: A shared way in which actions or customs communicate social meaning without needing a full verbal explanation.
brief.meaningZh: 行動或習俗傳達人際意思的共同方式，不必用完整說話解釋。
brief.grammar: act as/become a social language; explain which action communicates which meaning to which people.
brief.register: Creative language metaphor for social practices, not a claim that one gesture has the same meaning across all groups.
brief.boundaryZh: 需具體情境及理解者，不把一個家庭或群體的意思推成普遍規則。
brief.misconceptionZh: 看見行動不必然知道動機；可問當事人怎理解。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述習俗的人際作用，並保留文化或個人差異。

options.en: A meal practice communicated consideration within that family.
options.zh: 一項吃飯做法，在這家庭傳達體諒。

options.en: Only an instruction about how much food each person must eat.
options.zh: 只指示每人必須吃多少。

options.en: The meal began before the family checked whether everyone had a bowl.
options.zh: 家人沒查人人有碗前，已開始吃飯。

options.en: A rule for visiting guests only, not for the family members at the table.
options.zh: 只給訪客、不給同席家人的規矩。

listening.explanationZh: 人人有碗才開始，傳達這家庭不漏人的關懷；不是只限訪客或規定份量。
listening.en: In the family in our story, waiting until everyone had a bowl acted as a social language of care: it showed that nobody was being left out before the meal began.
listening.zh: 在故事這家庭，等人人有碗才開始，是關懷的社交語言：開飯前表明不漏下任何人。

reply.promptEn: What did waiting for everyone’s bowl communicate in that family?
reply.promptZh: 在這家庭，等人人有碗傳達甚麼？

options.en: It showed that the meal should include each person.
options.zh: 它表示用餐應包含每個人。

options.en: It acted as a social language of care by making sure nobody was left out.
options.zh: 它確保不漏下任何人，成為關懷的社交語言。

options.en: The shared practice expressed consideration without a long explanation.
options.zh: 共同做法不用長解釋，也表達體諒。

options.en: The action made belonging visible before anyone started eating.
options.zh: 開始吃前，行動讓歸屬感看得見。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都連到在場每人有份，不預設其他家庭同樣理解。

scene.promptZh: 劇團老成員開排練前，總留一張空椅給新來的人，並解釋是歡迎加入的做法。哪句貼切？

options.en: The small ritual acts as a social language of welcome in this group.
options.zh: 小儀式在這組成為歡迎的社交語言。

options.en: The chair proves the newcomer has already accepted a permanent role.
options.zh: 空椅證明新人已接受永久職位。

options.en: The group uses the empty chair only to keep visitors outside.
options.zh: 小組只用空椅把訪客留門外。

scene.explanationZh: 老成員已解釋歡迎意思，不是任命或拒入。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 a social language 自行推出？

options.en: Actions can communicate shared social meanings.
options.zh: 行動可傳達共同人際意思。

options.en: The same action must carry an identical message in every setting.
options.zh: 同一行動在每個環境必傳相同意思。

options.en: Understanding may depend on local practice and explanation.
options.zh: 理解可能依賴本地做法及解釋。

contrast.explanationZh: 意思需放回群體及情境，不能預設普遍相同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想把故事家庭等碗的做法，寫成所有家庭都遵守；你只有這家的解釋。哪句較好？

options.en: It is a social language of care in this family; we should ask how other households understand similar actions.
options.zh: 它在這家是關懷的社交語言；其他家庭怎理解相似行動，應再問。

options.en: This family’s explanation establishes the same meaning for households we have not observed.
options.zh: 這家解釋已確立未觀察家庭也有同一意思。

options.en: Then the waiting was merely a delay, rather than a gesture the family understood.
options.zh: 那麼等候只是延誤，不是家人理解的行動意思。

dialogue.explanationZh: 一個家庭的意思可描述，未觀察家庭仍需資料；也不因不能普遍化，就把這家理解的行動當純延誤。

speaking.en: The gesture acted as a social language in that group, where its meaning had been shared and explained.
speaking.zh: 那動作在意思已共同理解並獲解釋的群體，成為一種社交語言。
speaking.promptZh: 你想連結行動、意思與群體。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你加入讀書會，成員每次反對前，先用自己的話確認對方意思。主持人解釋這是表達尊重的做法，不表示同意。你想給下一位新人寫簡介，用一至兩句英文說明這套習慣的人際意思。

examples.en: Repeating the other person’s point before disagreeing acts as a social language of respect in this reading group. It shows that the view has been heard, not that everyone agrees with it.
examples.zh: 這讀書會反對前先覆述對方觀點，是尊重的社交語言；它表示已聽見，不表示大家同意。

examples.en: The group uses a social language of respect by checking each view before challenging it. The host explained that this habit makes careful listening visible while leaving room for disagreement.
examples.zh: 小組挑戰觀點前先核意思，以此作尊重的社交語言；主持人解釋，習慣讓仔細聆聽看得見，也保留不同意空間。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以反對前先確認意思的具體做法，說明尊重與聆聽，不把尊重誤作同意；介紹限定這個已獲主持人解釋的讀書會。

takeaways.en: Their habit of introducing every helper by name became a social language of recognition at the club.
takeaways.zh: 俱樂部逐一叫名介紹幫手的習慣，成為表達肯定的社交語言。

takeaways.en: In her account, sharing the first story acted as a social language that invited others into the conversation.
takeaways.zh: 她的敘述中，先分享第一個故事是邀大家加入對話的社交語言。

lessons.titleEn: grow out of real daily life
lessons.titleZh: 從真實日常經驗發展出來

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Customs often grow out of real daily life.
sources.expression: grow out of real daily life

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Their arrangement grows out of choice and practicality.
sources.expression: grows out of choice and practicality

brief.meaningEn: Develop from an existing experience, need or situation.
brief.meaningZh: 由已有經驗、需要或情況發展而來。
brief.grammar: grow out of + source; grew/grown; in this lesson develop-from, not become too old or too large for something.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb with a development sense; the source adds real daily life as its particular origin.
brief.boundaryZh: 需要來源與發展的連結，不是凡時間較早都必定造成後來結果。
brief.misconceptionZh: 與長大後不再合身的outgrow意思不同，也不把習俗一概說成專家先設計。
brief.outcomeZh: 能交代實際需要怎逐步形成做法，保留因果依據。

options.en: An everyday access problem caused by different arrival times.
options.zh: 不同抵達時間造成的日常進門問題。

options.en: A complete routine imposed before anyone experienced an access problem.
options.zh: 未有人遇進門問題前，已被強加的完整做法。

options.en: The old routine ended because nobody needed access at different times.
options.zh: 舊做法結束，因沒有人需要在不同時間進門。

options.en: The shifts changed only after the collection system had been abandoned.
options.zh: 領取安排取消後，輪班才改。

listening.explanationZh: 不同班及先到者進不了門，促成領取點與留言；不是原先無需求或新系統取消後才改班。
listening.en: Our shared key routine grew out of real daily life: different shifts meant someone often arrived before the key-holder, so we agreed a collection point and a simple message system.
listening.zh: 共用鎖匙做法從真實日常發展出來：不同輪班讓人常比持匙者先到，所以我們議定領取點與簡單留言安排。

reply.promptEn: Why did you create a key collection point and message system?
reply.promptZh: 你們為甚麼設鎖匙領取點及留言安排？

options.en: Different arrival times made access difficult when the key-holder was not there.
options.zh: 持匙者不在時，不同抵達時間令進門困難。

options.en: The routine grew out of the ordinary problem of arriving before the key-holder.
options.zh: 做法從比持匙者先到的日常問題發展而來。

options.en: We built an arrangement around a difficulty people had actually experienced.
options.zh: 我們按大家實際遇過的困難建立安排。

options.en: A practical need led us to agree how keys and messages would be handled.
options.zh: 實際需要讓我們議定怎處理鎖匙及留言。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都給日常需要與安排的連結，不憑單純先後推因果。

scene.promptZh: 學校圖書角新人常問哪裏借筆、怎留書位，同學便把這些實際問題整理成簡單指南。哪句準確？

options.en: The guide grew out of the practical questions newcomers kept asking.
options.zh: 指南從新人反覆提出的實際問題發展而來。

options.en: The guide was completed before any newcomer asked those questions.
options.zh: 任何新人提出那些問題前，指南已完成。

options.en: The guide was created only to display artwork, not to answer practical questions.
options.zh: 指南只為展示畫作，不為回答實際問題。

scene.explanationZh: 新人問題是指南的實際來源；不是先完成再有人問，也不是純展示畫作。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 grow out of 的來源發展意思？

options.en: A practice develops in response to an experienced need.
options.zh: 做法因應經歷過的需要發展。

options.en: A child becomes too large for a coat.
options.zh: 孩子長大，外套不再合身。

options.en: A creative idea develops from repeated observations.
options.zh: 創意從反覆觀察發展。

contrast.explanationZh: 外套不合身是另一個grow-out-of意思，不是本課來源發展。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友只因留言安排在輪班後出現，就說已證明原因；你還有大家說常先到門外的記錄。哪句最好？

options.en: The routine grew out of that access problem; the arrival records explain the link, not just the order of dates.
options.zh: 做法從進門問題發展而來；抵達記錄解釋連結，不只日期先後。

options.en: The order of dates alone is enough to explain why the system developed.
options.zh: 單靠日期先後，已足夠解釋系統為何發展。

options.en: The group introduced the message system before any shift-related access problem occurred.
options.zh: 任何輪班進門問題出現前，小組已引入留言系統。

dialogue.explanationZh: 抵達記錄說明需要怎引出安排；只看日期不足以解釋原因，也不能改成問題前已設好。

speaking.en: The idea grew out of an everyday difficulty, and we can explain how that experience led to the new arrangement.
speaking.zh: 構思從日常困難發展，我們也能解釋經驗怎引出新安排。
speaking.promptZh: 你想交代來源及因果連結。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫詩，每天搭火車聽到車輪重複聲，慢慢形成一段詩的節奏；後來你按停站的短暫安靜調整斷行。用一至兩句英文說明創作來源，不說火車替你寫好全詩。

examples.en: The poem’s rhythm grew out of real daily life, especially the repeated sound of the train wheels. I used the quiet at each stop to rethink the line breaks.
examples.zh: 詩的節奏從真實日常發展，尤其車輪重複聲；我用每站短暫安靜重新考慮斷行。

examples.en: My line breaks grew out of listening to the journey, rather than copying a ready-made pattern. The sounds gave me a starting point that I still had to shape.
examples.zh: 我的斷行從聽旅程發展，不是照抄現成模式；聲音給起點，仍需我塑造。

writing.selfCheckZh: 連結聽到的聲音、停站安靜與詩節奏及斷行，保留作者加工，不把來源當已完成作品。

takeaways.en: The workshop’s reminder system grew out of repeated questions from first-time visitors.
takeaways.zh: 工房提醒安排，從初訪者反覆提問發展而來。

takeaways.en: Her story grew out of the conversations she heard while helping at the station.
takeaways.zh: 她的故事從車站幫忙時聽到的對話發展而來。

Final poetic process changes mechanism from solving shared access logistics.

lessons.titleZh: 餐桌旁並非隨意的點綴

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Manners are not random decorations around a meal.

brief.meaningEn: An image for meal practices treated as superficial extras without meaning, often rejected by saying they are not such decorations.
brief.meaningZh: 把餐桌做法看成無意思的表面點綴的意象；常用否定，指出其實有作用。
brief.grammar: manners/customs are not random decorations around a meal; plural decorations agrees with a plural subject; explain the practical or social role.
brief.register: Creative decoration metaphor. Here decorations means supposedly superficial practices, not actual flowers or ornaments.
brief.boundaryZh: 否定很重要；說不是隨意點綴，不表示每項習俗都必好或不能改。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需解釋具體作用，不只因習俗存在就稱必要。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把餐桌習慣與其人際或實際用途連起。

listening.promptZh: 說話者否定了哪個看法？

options.en: That the customs were merely superficial extras without a role.
options.zh: 習俗只是沒有作用的表面點綴。

options.en: That the bowls were passed in a shared order.
options.zh: 碗有共同傳遞次序。

options.en: That younger guests were included in the arrangement.
options.zh: 安排包含年幼客人。

options.en: That the family had any serving customs to explain.
options.zh: 家庭有可解釋的分菜習俗。

listening.explanationZh: not否定只有表面點綴，後文用參與及不漏人解釋用途。
listening.en: In this household, the serving customs were not random decorations around a meal: passing the bowls in order helped younger guests know when to join in without being overlooked.
listening.zh: 在這家庭，分菜習慣不是餐旁隨意點綴：依次傳碗讓年幼客人知道何時參與，不會被漏下。

reply.promptEn: Why did you say those serving customs mattered?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼說那些分菜習慣重要？

options.en: They helped younger guests understand when to join in.
options.zh: 它們幫年幼客人知道何時參與。

options.en: They were not random decorations around a meal; they made participation easier.
options.zh: 它們不是餐旁隨意點綴，而是讓參與較容易。

options.en: The order had a practical role in including people.
options.zh: 次序在讓大家有份上有實際作用。

options.en: I could explain what the custom did rather than call it an empty formality.
options.zh: 我能解釋習俗的作用，不只稱空洞形式。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋用途，沒有把每項習俗都稱不可改。

scene.promptZh: 一段故事說用餐前簡短介紹，幫不熟的客人認識誰與誰同住；作者想否定這只是無用形式。哪句合適？

options.en: The introductions are not random decorations around a meal; they help guests understand the company.
options.zh: 介紹不是餐旁隨意點綴，而是幫客人認識同席者。

options.en: The introductions named only the dishes, not the people at the table.
options.zh: 介紹只列菜名，不是同席者。

options.en: The introductions were added only to delay the meal, not to help guests recognise one another.
options.zh: 介紹只為拖延用餐，不為幫客人認識彼此。

scene.explanationZh: 情境是介紹同席者，幫客人理解彼此關係；不是只介紹菜式，也不是純為延誤。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 not random decorations around a meal 推出？

options.en: The speaker sees a role beyond a superficial extra.
options.zh: 說話者看見超出表面點綴的作用。

options.en: Every existing custom must be preserved without discussion.
options.zh: 每項既有習俗都必須不經討論保留。

options.en: Further context should explain why the practice matters.
options.zh: 更多情境應解釋做法為何重要。

contrast.explanationZh: 有用途不等於全部不可討論或改動。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想把依次分菜寫成純裝飾，但你知道它幫年幼客人知道何時參與。哪句較好？

options.en: They are not random decorations around a meal; the order helps younger guests take part.
options.zh: 它們不是餐旁隨意點綴；次序幫年幼客人參與。

options.en: The formal appearance is all that matters when describing the order, not who it helps.
options.zh: 描述次序只需看正式外觀，不看它幫誰。

options.en: We can omit the passing order because the younger guests already know when to join.
options.zh: 年幼客人早已知何時參與，所以可省傳遞次序。

dialogue.explanationZh: 題目說次序幫年幼客人參與，應解釋實際用途；只評外觀或假定他們早知，都未回應這作用。

speaking.en: The customs were not random decorations around a meal; each had a role that the family could explain.
speaking.zh: 習俗不是餐旁隨意點綴；每項都有家庭能解釋的作用。
speaking.promptZh: 你想保留否定並說明用途。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫短劇，飯桌上誰先開口、誰等人分菜，逐漸顯出一家人對年幼成員的期待；你要在創作筆記說這些動作幫觀眾理解關係，不只是把場面填滿，也不把一幕推成所有家庭。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: The small rituals are not random decorations around a meal in this scene; they reveal what the family expects from its younger members. I want the audience to notice those relationships through the pauses and turns.
examples.zh: 這幕的小儀式不是餐旁隨意點綴，而是顯出家庭對年幼成員的期待；我想觀眾透過停頓及輪次留意關係。

examples.en: These actions are not random decorations around a meal: who speaks first and who waits helps tell the family story. The scene concerns this household, not a rule for every family.
examples.zh: 這些動作不是餐旁隨意點綴：誰先說、誰等候，幫忙說這家的故事；場面關乎這家庭，不是所有家庭的規則。

writing.selfCheckZh: 將餐桌動作連到戲劇關係及觀眾理解的創作目標，保留這家庭的範圍，不把純存在當必有好作用。

takeaways.en: The greetings were not random decorations around a meal; they gave the host a chance to include the new guests.
takeaways.zh: 招呼不是餐旁隨意點綴，而是讓主人有機會包含新客人。

takeaways.en: Their customs were not random decorations around a meal, as the grandmother explained when she showed us how the dishes were shared.
takeaways.zh: 祖母示範怎分享菜時解釋，他們的習俗不是餐旁隨意點綴。

review.author: AI author source_inventory

english.evidence: Exact creative negative decoration construction retained. Final writing changes to dramaturgical choices and relationship cues, rather than another real serving arrangement; no blanket claim that customs must remain.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese checked against English subjects, negation, tense and modality; no independent human approval claimed.

lessons.titleZh: 對同一社交時刻有不同解讀

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Two guests may be reading the same social moment differently.

brief.meaningEn: Interpret the meaning of the same interpersonal interaction, possibly through different expectations.
brief.meaningZh: 對同一人際互動的意思作理解，可能受到不同期待影響。
brief.grammar: read/reading the same social moment; often differently; read is a perception metaphor rather than reading printed text.
brief.register: Creative social-reading phrase. Different interpretations should be grounded in the participants’ accounts, not assigned to a culture from appearance alone.
brief.boundaryZh: 同一行動可以有不同理解，但不等於任何解讀都有同等證據；可以問清意圖。
brief.misconceptionZh: 避免把一家或個人的期待說成整個文化必然如此。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述具體解讀差異並提出核對。

options.en: The guests interpreted the same offer in different ways.
options.zh: 客人對同一提議有不同理解。

options.en: The guests received different meals at different gatherings.
options.zh: 客人在不同聚會收到不同餐點。

options.en: Both guests had already explained that the offer felt equally welcome.
options.zh: 兩位客人早已說提議同樣受歡迎。

options.en: The host refused to ask about either person’s preference.
options.zh: 主人拒問任何人的偏好。

listening.explanationZh: 同一添食提議，關心與壓力兩種感受，後來詢問作核對。
listening.en: When the host offered another serving, one guest heard care while the other felt pressure; they were reading the same social moment differently, so the host asked what each person preferred.
listening.zh: 主人再添食時，一位客人理解為關心，另一位感到壓力；他們對同一社交時刻有不同解讀，所以主人問各人偏好。

reply.promptEn: Why did the host ask about preferences rather than assume the offer was welcome?
reply.promptZh: 主人為甚麼問偏好，不假定添食受歡迎？

options.en: The guests had expressed different reactions to the same offer.
options.zh: 客人對同一提議表達不同反應。

options.en: They were reading the same social moment differently, and the host wanted to clarify.
options.zh: 他們對同一社交時刻解讀不同，主人想問清。

options.en: What felt caring to one person felt pressuring to the other.
options.zh: 對一人像關心，對另一人卻像壓力。

options.en: Asking would help distinguish her intention from how each guest received it.
options.zh: 詢問可分清她的意圖及各客人怎接收。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以已說的差異解釋核對需要，不作群體刻板推論。

scene.promptZh: 同伴笑了一下，一人以為他在嘲諷，另一人以為只是鬆一口氣；兩人都想先問清。哪句貼切？

options.en: They are reading the same social moment differently.
options.zh: 他們對同一社交時刻作不同解讀。

options.en: They have observed two separate incidents on different days.
options.zh: 他們觀察了不同日子的兩件事。

options.en: Both have confirmed that the laugh was intended as mockery.
options.zh: 兩人都已確認笑意在嘲諷。

scene.explanationZh: 同一笑聲仍有兩種未確認理解，不能改成別日事件或確認動機。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 reading the same social moment differently 得出？

options.en: The participants may interpret one interaction in different ways.
options.zh: 參與者可能對同一互動作不同理解。

options.en: One participant’s nationality alone explains the interpretation.
options.zh: 只憑某人的國籍，便可解釋其理解。

options.en: Asking about intention and experience may clarify the difference.
options.zh: 問意圖及體驗，可能幫釐清差異。

contrast.explanationZh: 需個人及情境資料，不以身份代替解釋。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想由客人感壓力，就斷言主人故意強迫；主人原想關心，現在願問偏好。哪句最好？

options.en: They were reading the same social moment differently: the host intended care, but the guest felt pressure, so asking preferences would help.
options.zh: 他們對同一時刻解讀不同：主人原想關心，客人卻感壓力，問偏好會有幫助。

options.en: The guest felt pressure, so the host must have intended to force another serving.
options.zh: 客人感壓力，所以主人一定原想強迫再添食。

options.en: Then the guest should be recorded as welcoming the offer because the host meant well.
options.zh: 那麼既然主人好意，就把客人寫成歡迎添食。

dialogue.explanationZh: 主人關心的意圖與客人感壓力，可同時保留；不能用反應代替意圖，也不能用好意抹去壓力。

speaking.en: They were reading the same social moment differently, so a direct question helped clarify what each person meant.
speaking.zh: 他們對同一社交時刻解讀不同，所以直接詢問有助釐清各人意思。
speaking.promptZh: 你想保留兩面並問清。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：活動報到時，職員招手想請你補交文件，旁邊排隊者卻以為職員容許你先入場。你要說明兩人對同一動作的理解，並請職員向隊伍解釋流程，不責備對方無禮。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: We were reading the same social moment differently: the wave meant I should bring a missing document, not enter ahead of the queue. Could the staff member explain the procedure to everyone waiting?
examples.zh: 我們對同一社交時刻解讀不同：招手是叫我補文件，不是先進場。職員可向等候者解釋流程嗎？

examples.en: The people in the queue were reading the same social moment as permission for early entry, while I had been asked to complete the paperwork. A clear explanation would help us understand the same process.
examples.zh: 排隊者把同一時刻解作容許先入場，我卻是獲叫補文件；清楚解釋可幫大家理解同一流程。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把招手的工作用途與旁人看到的優先進場分開，請職員說流程；不是假定排隊者已知全部資料或故意找麻煩。

takeaways.en: They were reading the same social moment differently when a long pause felt thoughtful to one and dismissive to the other.
takeaways.zh: 長停頓令一人覺得在思考、另一人覺得被敷衍時，他們對同一社交時刻解讀不同。

takeaways.en: I asked what the invitation meant because we seemed to be reading the same social moment in different ways.
takeaways.zh: 我們似乎對同一社交時刻有不同理解，所以我問邀請意思。

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese checked against English subjects, negation, tense and modality; no independent human approval claimed.

lessons.titleZh: 映照群體文化的小鏡子

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The family meal is a small cultural mirror.

brief.meaningEn: A small practice or event that reflects some wider values or habits of a particular group.
brief.meaningZh: 一項小做法或活動，映照特定群體某些較廣的價值或習慣。
brief.grammar: act as/be a small cultural mirror; identify the practice, the group and the observed values.
brief.register: Creative mirror metaphor. A limited example can suggest a cultural pattern but cannot represent an entire population on its own.
brief.boundaryZh: 鏡子意象不代替證據，不把一個家庭或活動當整個社會的完整代表。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要指出觀察到甚麼及可推多遠，必要時再找其他人或例子比較。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體小事討論群體價值，清楚保留範圍。

options.en: A stated value in that household, shown through who was invited to speak.
options.zh: 透過邀誰先說，顯示這家庭的某項價值。

options.en: A complete description of every household in the country.
options.zh: 全國每個家庭的完整描述。

options.en: Only the table’s appearance, without any connection to who was invited to speak.
options.zh: 只指桌面外觀，與邀誰說話無關。

options.en: A rule excluding younger people from the family conversation.
options.zh: 把年幼者排除在家庭對話外的規矩。

listening.explanationZh: 邀最年幼者先說故事，映照家中重視各代的價值；不是只評外觀、全國完整規則或排除年幼者。
listening.en: The meal was a small cultural mirror of that household: the family invited the youngest person to tell the first story, reflecting the importance they placed on hearing each generation.
listening.zh: 那餐像映照這家庭文化的小鏡子：家人請最年幼者先講故事，反映他們重視聽不同世代。

reply.promptEn: Why did that small meal detail interest you?
reply.promptZh: 那個小小用餐細節為甚麼引起你注意？

options.en: It showed how this family made space for different generations.
options.zh: 它顯示這家怎為不同世代留空間。

options.en: It was a small cultural mirror of the value they placed on hearing the youngest voice.
options.zh: 它像文化小鏡子，映照他們重視最年幼者聲音。

options.en: The speaking order gave a concrete example of a wider household value.
options.zh: 說話次序給一個具體例子，反映較廣的家庭價值。

options.en: I could connect the observed action with what the family said mattered to them.
options.zh: 我能把所見行動，連到家人明說重視的事。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以小做法與已說價值連結，不將一餐當全國代表。

scene.promptZh: 俱樂部周年會逐一介紹幕後幫手，負責人說這延續他們重視共同貢獻的習慣。哪句貼切？

options.en: The introductions act as a small cultural mirror of this club’s values.
options.zh: 介紹像文化小鏡子，映照這俱樂部的價值。

options.en: The event establishes how every organisation recognises volunteers.
options.zh: 活動確立每個機構怎肯定義工。

options.en: The introductions show that only the chair’s work matters to the club.
options.zh: 介紹顯示俱樂部只重視主席工作。

scene.explanationZh: 逐一介紹及負責人解釋，支持這組共同貢獻價值，不推所有機構。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 a small cultural mirror 自行得出？

options.en: A practice may reveal something about a group’s values.
options.zh: 做法可能顯示群體一些價值。

options.en: One observation fully represents everyone in a broad population.
options.zh: 一次觀察完整代表廣大群體的每人。

options.en: The claim should be checked against its actual scope and evidence.
options.zh: 說法應按實際範圍及證據核對。

contrast.explanationZh: 小例子不能無條件代表全體。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想從你觀察的一家用餐次序，寫成全國家庭的共同規則；你沒有其他家庭資料。哪句最好？

options.en: It is a small cultural mirror of this household; we need more accounts before making a wider claim.
options.zh: 它像映照這家庭的文化小鏡子；作更廣說法前，需更多敘述。

options.en: This one meal gives enough evidence to describe how households elsewhere behave.
options.zh: 只憑這一餐，已足以描述別處家庭的行為。

options.en: Then the meal cannot tell us anything about this family unless it represents the whole country.
options.zh: 那麼除非代表全國，這餐就不能告訴我們任何這家的事。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可保留有限觀察的意義，同時拒絕未有資料的普遍化。

speaking.en: The event was a small cultural mirror of that group, rather than a complete picture of every community.
speaking.zh: 活動像映照那群體的文化小鏡子，不是每個社群的完整圖像。
speaking.promptZh: 你想提出有範圍的文化觀察。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你整理街坊節慶的舊照片與口述訪問，發現大家每年修補布旗再用；主辦者說這反映珍惜材料及傳下手藝。你想寫這項修補習慣反映的本地價值，也比較其他參加者的回憶。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: The repaired banners are a small cultural mirror of this festival’s habit of reusing materials. I will compare the organiser’s explanation with other participants’ memories of the repairs.
examples.zh: 修補布旗像文化小鏡子，映照這節慶重用材料的習慣；我會把主辦者解釋與其他參加者的修補回憶比較。

examples.en: Repairing the old banners offers a small cultural mirror of the group’s care for materials and shared skills. The photographs and interviews help us examine that practice without treating it as a rule for every festival.
examples.zh: 修舊布旗像文化小鏡子，映照這組珍惜材料及共同手藝；照片與訪問幫我們檢視做法，不把它當每個節慶的規則。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把每年修旗、主辦者解釋及其他參加者回憶連起，討論珍惜材料及手藝的有限文化觀察，不從單一活動推全體。

takeaways.en: The visitors’ book became a small cultural mirror of the club’s habit of recognising each helper.
takeaways.zh: 訪客冊像文化小鏡子，映照俱樂部逐一肯定幫手的習慣。

takeaways.en: Their shared meal offered a small cultural mirror of the way that household welcomed new members.
takeaways.zh: 共餐像文化小鏡子，映照這家庭怎歡迎新成員。

brief.meaningEn: Make something from its beginning rather than adapt an existing finished version or draft; in cooking, make the dish or sauce rather than simply use a ready-made one.
brief.meaningZh: 從頭製作，不直接改現成版本或原稿；煮食時可指自行做菜或醬，而非直接用現成成品。
brief.grammar: make/build/write something from scratch; start from scratch; specify the product or draft being made, not the origin of every basic ingredient or tool.
brief.register: Established idiom. From scratch may still use prepared basic ingredients, tools and prior knowledge; it does not require making every ingredient or tool oneself.
brief.boundaryZh: 從頭做不表示不用工具或既有知識，也不自動比重用版本好。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要說清不用哪種現成起點，不把每個基本工具也當需親手製造。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述從頭製作的範圍及所需安排。

options.en: Creating a new booklet rather than reusing the unsuitable template.
options.zh: 新做小冊，不重用不合適範本。

options.en: Changing only the title on the old building’s booklet.
options.zh: 只改舊樓小冊的標題。

options.en: Writing new drawing software was included in the booklet project before the design could begin.
options.zh: 小冊項目包括先寫新繪圖軟件，才可開始設計。

options.en: Using the old room descriptions without asking staff to check them.
options.zh: 不請職員核對，沿用舊房間描述。

listening.explanationZh: 不用舊範本是起點，仍可用軟件及核對，並非從零發明所有工具。
listening.en: We built the welcome booklet from scratch because the old template described a different building; we still used the usual drawing software and asked staff to check the room names.
listening.zh: 舊範本寫的是另一幢樓，我們從頭做歡迎小冊；仍用平常繪圖軟件，也請職員核房名。

reply.promptEn: Why did you make a new booklet instead of adapting the old template?
reply.promptZh: 你們為甚麼新做小冊，不改舊範本？

options.en: The old one described a different building and would not provide the right structure.
options.zh: 舊版寫另一幢樓，不能提供合適結構。

options.en: We worked from scratch because the earlier template did not fit this building.
options.zh: 早先範本不合這樓，我們便從頭做。

options.en: We needed a new starting design, with the room information checked by staff.
options.zh: 我們需新設計起點，房間資料另由職員核對。

options.en: Reusing the old descriptions would carry the wrong building into the guide.
options.zh: 重用舊描述會把錯樓資料帶入指南。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代不重用範本的理由，不把新做說成拒絕軟件或請教。

scene.promptZh: 人物為短片寫全新旋律，沒有改編舊曲，仍用家中鋼琴試音。哪句準確？

options.en: She is composing the melody from scratch while using the piano as a tool.
options.zh: 她從頭創作旋律，同時用鋼琴作工具。

options.en: She is arranging an existing folk tune for a different instrument.
options.zh: 她把已有民歌改編給另一樂器。

options.en: She is only changing the title of a finished song.
options.zh: 她只改完成歌曲的標題。

scene.explanationZh: 新旋律是從頭製作的作品，鋼琴可作既有工具；不是改編舊曲或只改標題。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 made it from scratch 推斷？

options.en: A ready-made version was not used as the starting product.
options.zh: 沒有以現成版本作產品起點。

options.en: The maker used no tools or knowledge developed by anyone else.
options.zh: 製作者沒用任何人發展的工具或知識。

options.en: Context should specify what was newly made.
options.zh: 情境應指出新做甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 工具與知識仍可使用，需按製作範圍理解。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說不用舊範本就連繪圖軟件也不能用，你只想新做適合樓宇的小冊。哪句最好？

options.en: Making the booklet from scratch means creating a new design here, not rejecting the tools we use to draw it.
options.zh: 這裏從頭做小冊是新設計，不是拒用繪圖工具。

options.en: Using the familiar software means we are still adapting the old booklet.
options.zh: 用熟悉軟件，便表示我們仍在修改舊小冊。

options.en: Then changing the title alone would count as a wholly new booklet.
options.zh: 那麼只改標題，也算全新小冊。

dialogue.explanationZh: 同一工具可新做另一設計，不能把工具重用當範本重用，也不能只改標題就當全新。

speaking.en: We made the guide from scratch, while still using familiar tools and checking the details with other people.
speaking.zh: 我們從頭做指南，仍用熟悉工具，也向別人核細節。
speaking.promptZh: 你想說清從頭製作的範圍。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：小說人物想學做祖母的醬汁，祖母給基本食材及步驟，不用現成樽裝醬；人物仍會用家中鍋及請祖母示範，先試一小份。用一至兩句英文說明做法。

examples.en: I want to make the sauce from scratch with the ingredients my grandmother listed, rather than begin with a bottled sauce. I will try a small batch and ask her to show me the first step.
examples.zh: 我想按祖母列的食材從頭做醬，不從樽裝醬開始；會先試小份，請她示範首步。

examples.en: Making it from scratch does not mean working without help. I can use the family pan and learn the steps from my grandmother.
examples.zh: 從頭做不表示不能求助；我可用家中鍋，向祖母學步驟。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說清不用現成醬，但可用既有鍋及示範；從頭製作的範圍不需延伸成無工具或無幫助。

takeaways.en: She wrote the invitation from scratch because the old letter addressed a different audience.
takeaways.zh: 舊信寫給不同讀者，她便從頭寫邀請。

takeaways.en: They made the sauce from scratch and kept notes on the steps they wanted to ask about.
takeaways.zh: 他們從頭做醬，也記下想請教的步驟。

brief.meaningEn: Reduce how much of something is used or done.
brief.meaningZh: 減少使用某物的量，或做某事的次數。
brief.grammar: cut back on + noun/-ing; cut is present and past, cutting is progressive; reduction need not mean stopping completely.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb; specify what is reduced and retain any stated remaining use.
brief.boundaryZh: 減少不等於一律停用，也不自動保證主要目標已達；需交代比較基準。
brief.misconceptionZh: 分清用量、次數及內容質素，不把少做一項當沒有工作。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出具體減量並保留必要部分。

listening.promptZh: 減少了甚麼，仍保留甚麼？

options.en: Routine printed notices were reduced, with some copies retained for access needs.
options.zh: 例行紙本通知減少，仍為使用需要留一些。

options.en: Paper notices were stopped entirely for everyone.
options.zh: 所有人都完全停用紙本通知。

options.en: The group increased the number of routine printed updates.
options.zh: 小組增加例行更新印量。

options.en: Online updates were removed and replaced with more paper.
options.zh: 網上更新刪去，改更多紙本。

listening.explanationZh: while keeping 保留部分印本，cut back 是減量，不是全停。
listening.en: We cut back on printed rehearsal notices by posting routine updates on the shared board, while keeping a few paper copies for people who could not check it online.
listening.zh: 我們把例行更新貼共用板，減少印排練通知，但為不能上網查看的人保留少量紙本。

reply.promptEn: How did you reduce printing without excluding people who needed paper?
reply.promptZh: 你們怎減印，又不排除需要紙本的人？

options.en: We moved routine updates online but kept some copies available.
options.zh: 我們把例行更新放網上，仍留一些紙本。

options.en: We cut back on printed notices rather than remove them completely.
options.zh: 我們減少印通知，不是完全取消。

options.en: The main updates were shared digitally, with a small paper supply for those who needed it.
options.zh: 主要更新以數碼分享，另留少量紙本給有需要者。

options.en: We reduced the routine print run while keeping an access option.
options.zh: 我們減例行印量，同時保留一種使用選擇。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均保留減量及剩下用途，不把減少當取消。

scene.promptZh: 你們改為每周一份摘要，不再每天印同類紀錄，原始文件仍可查。哪句合適？

options.en: We cut back on daily printouts while keeping the original records available.
options.zh: 我們減少每日印本，仍保留原始紀錄可查。

options.en: We destroyed the original records so no one could consult them.
options.zh: 我們銷毀原始紀錄，沒人可查。

options.en: We now print the same records more frequently than before.
options.zh: 我們現在比以前更常印相同紀錄。

scene.explanationZh: 改摘要減印，未表示銷毀內容或加頻率。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 cut back on something 自行推斷？

options.en: Its amount or frequency is reduced.
options.zh: 它的量或頻率減少。

options.en: It has necessarily been eliminated completely.
options.zh: 它必定已完全消除。

options.en: A relevant earlier amount may provide the comparison.
options.zh: 可用相關早先用量比較。

contrast.explanationZh: 減量與全停不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友聽你減印，就把仍保留的紙本也下架；你們已說要留給不能上網的人。哪句最好？

options.en: We are cutting back on printing, not removing the paper option that some members still need.
options.zh: 我們減印，不是取消一些組員仍需的紙本選擇。

options.en: The reduced print run means we decided nobody needs paper any longer.
options.zh: 減印量表示我們已決定沒人再需紙本。

options.en: Then the online updates should be printed in full each day instead of using the summary.
options.zh: 那麼不用摘要，改把網上更新每日全部印出。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留原定使用需要，減量不是擅自取消或返回更大量。

speaking.en: We can cut back on the repeated work while keeping the part that people still need.
speaking.zh: 我們可減少重複工作，同時保留大家仍需要的部分。
speaking.promptZh: 你想交代減量及保留。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你剪一段舞台記錄片，開場用了很多相似廣角鏡頭，人物細節太遲出現；你想減少重複遠景，仍保留一個交代場地的鏡頭，再早一點進入人物。用一至兩句英文提出剪接。

examples.en: We should cut back on the repeated wide shots while keeping one to establish the room. That would let us reach the performer’s hands earlier.
examples.zh: 我們應減少重複廣角鏡頭，仍留一個交代房間，便可較早看到表演者雙手。

examples.en: Cutting back on similar opening shots could make space for the performer’s detail without losing the sense of place. I would keep the clearest view of the stage.
examples.zh: 減少相似開場鏡頭，可留空間看表演者細節，又不失場地感；我會留最清楚的舞台全景。

writing.selfCheckZh: 減少重複鏡頭，仍保留交代場地的一個，說明剪接目的；不把減量當所有全景都應刪。

takeaways.en: She cut back on repeated examples so the workshop had time for participants’ questions.
takeaways.zh: 她減少重複例子，讓工作坊有時間答參加者問題。

takeaways.en: We are cutting back on duplicate messages while keeping one clear reminder before the deadline.
takeaways.zh: 我們減少重複訊息，仍在期限前留一個清楚提醒。

sources.sentence: With better access, the tide may well turn.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: With better rules, the tide could turn for the river.

brief.meaningEn: The overall direction of a situation may change, often towards a more favourable outcome in context.
brief.meaningZh: 整體情況方向可能改變，情境中常指轉向較有利結果。
brief.grammar: the tide may well turn; may well suggests a real possibility or likelihood, not certainty; the tide could turn is a related modal form.
brief.register: Established sea-current metaphor for a trend changing direction. The speaker still needs evidence for the forecast.
brief.boundaryZh: 可能轉向不等於已逆轉或下一步必成功；應交代原趨勢與新跡象。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一個正面回應可作線索，但不能直接說長期走勢已確立。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出有根據而有限度的趨勢預測。

listening.promptZh: 說話者的判斷到了哪一步？

options.en: New interest gives a reason to hope for a change, conditional on return visits.
options.zh: 新興趣給轉變的希望，仍有持續回來的條件。

options.en: The earlier decline has already been reversed over many months.
options.zh: 早前下跌已持續多月被逆轉。

options.en: The new workshop attracted only the same returning members as before.
options.zh: 新工房只吸引原有回來的組員。

options.en: The speaker has confirmed that all first-time visitors will return.
options.zh: 說話者已確認所有初訪者都會回來。

listening.explanationZh: 新預約是跡象，if保留後續條件，may well不是已證明長期逆轉。
listening.en: Attendance had fallen for months, but the new evening workshop drew several first-time bookings, so the tide may well turn if those visitors keep coming back.
listening.zh: 出席人數連跌幾月，但新晚間工房有幾位首次預約者；若他們持續回來，趨勢可能轉向。

reply.promptEn: Why are you cautiously hopeful after the fall in attendance?
reply.promptZh: 出席下跌後，你為甚麼審慎有希望？

options.en: The evening session attracted new bookings, though return visits still matter.
options.zh: 晚場吸引新預約，但回訪仍重要。

options.en: The tide may well turn if the new visitors return, since the evening session has drawn fresh interest.
options.zh: 晚場帶來新興趣，若新訪客回來，趨勢可能轉向。

options.en: We have an encouraging sign rather than a settled long-term result.
options.zh: 我們有鼓舞跡象，不是已定長期結果。

options.en: The latest bookings suggest the new time could reach people the old sessions missed.
options.zh: 最新預約顯示新時間可能接觸舊場次未觸及的人。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均用新預約支持希望，也不把未來回訪當已確認。

scene.promptZh: 虛構比賽中，你們開局落後，改站位後連續創造兩次得分機會，但仍未追平。哪句準確表達有希望而未定結果？

options.en: The tide may well turn, though we are still behind and need to see whether the chances lead to points.
options.zh: 趨勢可能轉向，但我們仍落後，需看機會會否變成得分。

options.en: Those chances show that we have already won the match.
options.zh: 那些機會顯示我們已贏比賽。

options.en: The new chances came while our positioning stayed unchanged.
options.zh: 新機會出現時，我們站位仍沒改。

scene.explanationZh: 改站位後有新機會，是可能轉向的跡象；仍落後，未贏，也不能抹去站位改動。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 the tide may well turn 得出？

options.en: The speaker sees a meaningful possibility of changed direction.
options.zh: 說話者認為方向有實質轉變可能。

options.en: The change has already become a confirmed lasting result.
options.zh: 改變早已成為確認的持久結果。

options.en: The context should explain what signs support the possibility.
options.zh: 情境應解釋哪些跡象支持可能性。

contrast.explanationZh: 可能性與已確認的長期結果不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把首次預約寫成連續多月回升，你只知道新晚場開始有人查詢。哪句最好？

options.en: The tide may well turn, but we should track actual visits before reporting a sustained rise.
options.zh: 趨勢可能轉向，但報持續回升前，應追蹤實際到訪。

options.en: Each enquiry should be counted as a confirmed visit when reporting the rise.
options.zh: 報回升時，每項查詢都應算已確認到訪。

options.en: Perhaps we should report the enquiries as confirmed bookings instead of keeping the two figures separate.
options.zh: 或許應把查詢報成已確認預約，不把兩個數字分開。

dialogue.explanationZh: 查詢、預約與實際到訪應分清；新興趣可作跡象，不能提前當已到場或已定長期回升。

speaking.en: The tide may well turn if the new interest continues, but we do not yet have a lasting result.
speaking.zh: 若新興趣持續，趨勢可能轉向，但我們未有持久結果。
speaking.promptZh: 你想給有依據而保留條件的預測。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：小說人物一直被村民誤解，但公開了兩封能互相核對的信後，原先反對他的兩人願重新聽他說；其他人還未表態。你想寫輿論可能改變，而不是立刻人人支持。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: The tide may well turn now that two former critics are willing to hear him again. Their response is encouraging, but the rest of the village has not spoken.
examples.zh: 兩位曾批評的人願再聽他說，趨勢可能轉向；反應令人鼓舞，但其餘村民還未表態。

examples.en: The letters give him hope that the tide may well turn, rather than proof that the whole village now supports him. He still wants the others to examine the evidence.
examples.zh: 信件讓他有希望覺得趨勢可能轉向，不是全村已支持的證明；他仍想其餘人檢視證據。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用部分反對者願重聽作輿論改變的跡象，保留其餘人未表態及仍需檢視證據；不把希望當全體支持。

takeaways.en: After two groups offered help, the tide may well turn for the project, provided the promised work follows.
takeaways.zh: 兩組提出幫忙後，若承諾工作跟上，項目趨勢可能轉向。

takeaways.en: The tide could turn when readers see the missing letter, though the debate is still open.
takeaways.zh: 讀者看到欠缺信件時，趨勢可能轉向，但爭論仍未定。

lessons.titleZh: 把食物看作不只是燃料

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: We should see food not just as fuel but as part of family life.

brief.meaningEn: View food as having social, personal or cultural meaning as well as providing energy.
brief.meaningZh: 看食物既提供能量，也有人際、個人或文化意義。
brief.grammar: see/treat food not just as fuel but as + wider role; not just adds another dimension rather than denying the first.
brief.register: Creative food-as-fuel image with a not-just contrast. It does not deny nourishment or rank people’s ways of eating.
brief.boundaryZh: 不只是並非不是；肯定其他意義不表示能量或實際需要不重要。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需指出多出哪個層面，不只重複食物有價值，也不對別人的生活條件作道德判斷。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把基本用途與具體社會或個人意義並列。

options.en: A connection to shared memories alongside food’s basic sustaining role.
options.zh: 在食物基本維持作用以外，加入共同回憶的聯繫。

options.en: A claim that food has no role in sustaining the body.
options.zh: 聲稱食物沒有維持身體的作用。

options.en: An instruction to stop using the family recipes.
options.zh: 要求停用家庭食譜。

options.en: A statement that the memoir contains only lists of ingredients and no stories.
options.zh: 說回憶錄只有食材表，沒有故事。

listening.explanationZh: not just擴闊而非否定基本用途，食譜引故事是具體新增層面。
listening.en: In the family memoir, she sees food not just as fuel but as a way of keeping her father’s stories alive, because each shared recipe leads to memories they tell at the table.
listening.zh: 家族回憶錄中，她看食物不只是燃料，也是延續父親故事的方法，因每份共用食譜都引出飯桌上講的回憶。

reply.promptEn: Why does the memoir describe meals as more than simply eating?
reply.promptZh: 回憶錄為甚麼把餐飯描述為不只是吃？

options.en: The recipes bring the father’s stories into the shared meal.
options.zh: 食譜把父親故事帶進共餐。

options.en: She sees food not just as fuel but as a link to memories the family tells together.
options.zh: 她看食物不只是燃料，也是連起家人共說回憶的方式。

options.en: The meal gives those memories a place in family conversation.
options.zh: 餐飯為那些回憶在家庭對話留位置。

options.en: What they cook connects them with a person whose stories they want to keep.
options.zh: 煮甚麼把他們與想保留故事的那個人連起。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都提出食譜、故事及共同回憶的具體關係。

scene.promptZh: 一段文章說人物用熟悉菜式歡迎離鄉的朋友，朋友覺得有人記住自己的經歷；作者想加這人際層面。哪句合適？

options.en: The writer presents food not just as fuel but as a gesture of recognition.
options.zh: 作者把食物呈現為不只是燃料，也是肯定對方的行動。

options.en: The writer says the guest’s memories had no place in the meal.
options.zh: 作者說客人回憶在餐飯中沒位置。

options.en: The writer denies that people eat for any practical reason.
options.zh: 作者否定人吃東西有任何實際原因。

scene.explanationZh: 新增肯定及連繫層面，未否定其他實際作用。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 not just 的用法？

options.en: It keeps a basic role while adding another meaningful role.
options.zh: 保留基本作用，同時加入另一重要作用。

options.en: It denies the first role completely instead of adding to it.
options.zh: 完全否定首個作用，不是增加層面。

options.en: The following words can identify the added dimension.
options.zh: 後文可指出新增層面。

contrast.explanationZh: 不只是與完全不是不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴把回憶錄寫成食物不提供能量，你原本只是想加家庭回憶層面。哪句修訂最好？

options.en: She sees food not just as fuel but as a link to family memories; that adds meaning without denying its practical role.
options.zh: 她看食物不只是燃料，也是連繫家庭回憶的方法；這增加意義，沒有否定實際作用。

options.en: The paragraph concerns only memories and excludes food’s practical role.
options.zh: 段落只關回憶，不包括食物實際作用。

options.en: Then the account should contain only the ingredient amounts and leave out the father’s stories.
options.zh: 那麼只寫食材份量，不寫父親故事。

dialogue.explanationZh: not just保留基本作用並增加記憶層面；不是只談回憶，亦不是只列份量。

speaking.en: I see food not just as fuel but as part of the stories people share when they come together.
speaking.zh: 我看食物不只是燃料，也是在相聚時共說的故事一部分。
speaking.promptZh: 你想用不只是加入具體意義。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你策劃家庭食物記憶照片展，不只拍菜，也想拍磨舊的食譜、不同人的筆跡及共同備料的手，呈現記憶與勞動。用一至兩句英文寫選圖方向，不否定食物的基本作用。

examples.en: The exhibition should show food not just as fuel but as a record of memory and shared work. I would include the worn recipe book and the hands preparing the ingredients.
examples.zh: 展覽應呈現食物不只是燃料，也是記憶與共同工作的紀錄；我會加入磨舊食譜及備料的手。

examples.en: To present food not just as fuel, we can photograph the handwriting beside the recipes as well as the finished dishes. Those images would show who helped carry the family knowledge forward.
examples.zh: 為呈現食物不只是燃料，我們可拍食譜旁筆跡及完成菜式；圖片可顯示誰幫忙把家庭知識傳下去。

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出能在照片中看見的記憶、筆跡及勞動線索，將新增層面化成選圖決定，不把比喻當否定基本需要。

takeaways.en: The community project treated food not just as fuel but as a reason for neighbours to exchange family stories.
takeaways.zh: 社區項目看食物不只是燃料，也是街坊交換家族故事的契機。

takeaways.en: Her film shows food not just as fuel, following the people who pass their recipes to the next generation.
takeaways.zh: 她的影片追蹤傳食譜給下一代的人，呈現食物不只是燃料。

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese checked against English subjects, negation, tense and modality; no independent human approval claimed.

lessons.titleEn: what ends up on the plate
lessons.titleZh: 最後實際放到碟上的食物

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Shopping habits shape what ends up on the plate.
sources.expression: what ends up on the plate

brief.meaningEn: The food ultimately chosen, prepared or served after earlier decisions and circumstances.
brief.meaningZh: 經過早先決定及情況後，最終選來、做成或上桌的食物。
brief.grammar: what ends up on the plate; end up + place/result describes the final outcome; plate may summarise the meal in context.
brief.register: Natural final-outcome wording. The food may literally be on a plate; it need not be presented as an opaque idiom or a nutrition measurement.
brief.boundaryZh: 需分清原計劃與實際上桌結果，不由這說法補出食材、份量或健康結論。
brief.misconceptionZh: 最後結果可受多個步驟影響，不單憑一餐就判斷整體習慣。
brief.outcomeZh: 能追蹤前面選擇怎影響最後食物，並核對實際結果。

options.en: Ingredient availability changed what the family actually served.
options.zh: 食材供應改變家人實際上桌的菜。

options.en: The recipe guaranteed the exact planned dish despite the missing ingredient.
options.zh: 即使缺食材，食譜仍保證原計劃菜式。

options.en: The family made the original tomato dish after a neighbour supplied the missing ingredient.
options.zh: 鄰居補上欠食材後，家人做回原番茄菜。

options.en: The final dish was known before anyone checked the cupboard or the shop.
options.zh: 未查櫃及商店前，最終菜式已確定。

listening.explanationZh: 缺番茄與改用豆，把原食譜轉成另一道菜，不能只看計劃。
listening.en: The recipe was only one factor shaping what ends up on the plate: the shop had no tomatoes that evening, so the family used the beans already in the cupboard and served a different dish.
listening.zh: 食譜只是影響最後上碟食物的一項因素：那晚店裏沒番茄，所以家人用櫃中已有的豆，做了另一道菜。

reply.promptEn: Why did the meal differ from the recipe you first chose?
reply.promptZh: 餐飯為甚麼與最初選的食譜不同？

options.en: The shop lacked a needed ingredient, so we used what was available at home.
options.zh: 店缺所需食材，我們改用家中有的。

options.en: What ends up on the plate depends on the ingredients available as well as the recipe.
options.zh: 最後上碟食物除了食譜，也受現有食材影響。

options.en: We changed the dish after checking the shop and the cupboard.
options.zh: 查店及櫃後，我們改了菜。

options.en: The earlier plan did not account for the missing tomatoes.
options.zh: 較早計劃沒有計入缺番茄的情況。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都用缺食材及替代解釋計劃與結果差異。

scene.promptZh: 你原選一道需長時間烤的菜，但到家時才知只剩很短備餐時間，於是用現有材料做另一道。哪句準確？

options.en: The available time influenced what ends up on the plate, not just the recipe we liked.
options.zh: 現有時間影響最後上碟食物，不只看喜歡哪份食譜。

options.en: The planned recipe stayed unchanged because the family allowed the full cooking time.
options.zh: 家人留足煮食時間，所以原食譜沒改。

options.en: The family changed the recipe before knowing how much preparation time remained.
options.zh: 家人未知道剩多少備餐時間前，已改食譜。

scene.explanationZh: 先知道時間短，才用現有材料改菜；不是原食譜不改，或未知時間便先改。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 what ends up on the plate 推斷？

options.en: The account concerns the food ultimately served or chosen.
options.zh: 敘述關乎最後上桌或選擇的食物。

options.en: The original intention and final dish must be identical.
options.zh: 原本打算與最後菜式必定相同。

options.en: Earlier decisions may help explain the outcome.
options.zh: 較早決定可能幫解釋結果。

contrast.explanationZh: 這說法說最後結果，不保證計劃原樣實現。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴只把原食譜當已上桌結果，但你們當晚改用豆；你要準確寫記錄。哪句最好？

options.en: Let us record what ends up on the plate after the substitution, not just the recipe we intended to use.
options.zh: 我們記替代後最後上碟甚麼，不只記本想用的食譜。

options.en: The original tomato dish is what was served, because that was the recipe in the plan.
options.zh: 上桌的就是原番茄菜，因那是計劃中的食譜。

options.en: Then the cupboard ingredients were checked only after the original tomato dish had been served.
options.zh: 那麼原番茄菜上桌後，才查櫃內食材。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先缺番茄再查櫃用豆，應記替代後結果；不是原番茄菜已上桌，也不只列原計劃。

speaking.en: What ends up on the plate can differ from the first plan, so I want to record the actual choices as well.
speaking.zh: 最後上碟食物可能與最初計劃不同，所以我也想記實際選擇。
speaking.promptZh: 你想分清計劃與結果。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為學校餐廳做一日觀察，想比較餐牌介紹與學生實際取餐，並問學生為何略過某配菜；你尚未收資料，不可只看餐牌便寫學生吃了甚麼。用一至兩句英文提出觀察方法。

examples.en: We should observe what ends up on the plate rather than treat the menu as a record of each student’s meal. A short question could help explain why someone leaves out a side dish.
examples.zh: 我們應觀察最後上碟甚麼，不把餐牌當每位學生餐飯的紀錄；簡短提問可幫解釋為何有人略去配菜。

examples.en: To understand what ends up on the plate, I would compare the menu with actual selections and ask about one choice. I would not infer the whole meal from the description alone.
examples.zh: 要了解最後上碟甚麼，我會比餐牌與實際選取，並問一項選擇；不只憑介紹推斷整餐。

glossary.en: a record of each student’s meal

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出比較及提問的資料方法，保留還沒觀察的限制，不把餐牌當已吃結果或自行判健康。

takeaways.en: The family notes show how the shopping trip influenced what ends up on the plate.
takeaways.zh: 家庭筆記顯示購物怎影響最後上碟食物。

takeaways.en: We asked about the final choices because the menu alone did not tell us what ends up on the plate.
takeaways.zh: 我們問最後選擇，因單靠餐牌看不出實際上碟甚麼。

review.author: AI author source_inventory

english.evidence: Source figurative label retained in provenance; learner natural category recognises productive end-up outcome wording and possibly literal plate. Final observation-method task distinguishes offered menu from actual selection rather than another household ingredient substitution.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese checked against English subjects, negation, tense and modality; no independent human approval claimed.

lessons.titleEn: the fuel that keeps the body running
lessons.titleZh: 像燃料般支持身體活動

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Breakfast is the fuel that keeps the body running through school.
sources.expression: the fuel that keeps the body running

brief.meaningEn: A comparison of food providing energy for bodily activity with fuel keeping a machine operating.
brief.meaningZh: 把食物提供身體活動能量，比作燃料維持機器運作。
brief.grammar: describe food as the fuel that keeps the body running; kept can fit a past narrative; identify what fuel refers to.
brief.register: Creative body-as-machine metaphor. It is a simplified image, not a precise nutritional model or a claim about one food meeting every need.
brief.boundaryZh: running可指身體運作，不只跑步；意象不提供食物份量、成分或個人健康評估。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把燃料意象當成身體與引擎在所有方面完全相同。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋意象對應的有限意思，保留實際人物及活動。

options.en: Food viewed as a source of energy for continuing bodily activity.
options.zh: 把食物看作繼續身體活動的能量來源。

options.en: Petrol bought for a vehicle that carried the group’s equipment.
options.zh: 買給運器材車輛的汽油。

options.en: A description limited to competitive running rather than the walking trip.
options.zh: 只說競賽跑步，不關步行旅程。

options.en: A detailed calculation of each person’s nutritional needs.
options.zh: 每人營養需要的詳細計算。

listening.explanationZh: lunch 是意象指代，walking及背器材是活動；沒列汽油或營養計算。
listening.en: In his walking journal, he called lunch the fuel that kept the body running, then described the group eating before carrying their equipment to the next sketching stop.
listening.zh: 步行日記中，他把午餐叫作維持身體運作的燃料，再寫小組先吃東西，才背器材到下一個寫生點。

reply.promptEn: What did the narrator mean by calling lunch fuel?
reply.promptZh: 敘述者把午餐稱燃料，是甚麼意思？

options.en: He connected eating with the energy involved in continuing the walk.
options.zh: 他把吃東西與繼續步行所需能量連起。

options.en: He described lunch as the fuel that kept the body running during the outing.
options.zh: 他把午餐描述為外出時維持身體運作的燃料。

options.en: The machine image helped him describe the practical role of food on the trip.
options.zh: 機器意象幫他描述旅程中食物的實際作用。

options.en: He was using a comparison about food and activity, not reporting a petrol purchase.
options.zh: 他在比喻食物與活動，不是報買汽油。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋能量意象，不把它當精確飲食表。

scene.promptZh: 你整理兩段旅記索引：甲寫食物提供步行時能量，乙寫巴士在油站補油。要為甲選一句摘要，避免把兩種燃料混在一起。哪句適合？

options.en: The fuel that keeps the body running refers to food in the first account.
options.zh: 首段所說維持身體運作的燃料，指食物。

options.en: The first account records the bus receiving petrol at the station.
options.zh: 首段記巴士在油站加汽油。

options.en: Both accounts concern only refuelling vehicles, not food.
options.zh: 兩段都只關替車加油，不關食物。

scene.explanationZh: 索引需分甲的食物能量意象與乙的實際汽油，不互換資料，也不把兩段都歸車輛。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜把這個燃料意象當成？

options.en: A limited comparison about energy and bodily activity.
options.zh: 有關能量及身體活動的有限比較。

options.en: A complete account of an individual’s nutritional requirements.
options.zh: 個人營養需要的完整說明。

options.en: A way to make an abstract role easier to picture.
options.zh: 令抽象作用較易想像的方法。

contrast.explanationZh: 意象沒有所需個人資料或精確內容，不是完整評估。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把日記的燃料一詞寫成買了汽油，但段落明說午餐與步行。哪句修訂最好？

options.en: Keep lunch as the fuel that kept the body running; the paragraph uses a machine comparison for food.
options.zh: 保留午餐是維持身體運作的燃料；段落用機器意象寫食物。

options.en: The paragraph mainly concerns refuelling a vehicle that carries the equipment, rather than the group eating.
options.zh: 段落主要關運器材的車加油，不是小組吃東西。

options.en: Then running should be described as a race, rather than the body’s activity during the walk.
options.zh: 那麼running應寫成比賽，不是步行中身體活動。

dialogue.explanationZh: 原段有午餐及步行，fuel對應食物能量，running對應運作，不是車輛或跑步競賽。

speaking.en: He described food as the fuel that keeps the body running, using a simple image rather than a detailed nutritional explanation.
speaking.zh: 他用食物是維持身體運作的燃料這個簡單意象，不是詳細營養解釋。
speaking.promptZh: 你想解釋意象與限制。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替兒童解說圖片寫給插畫師的建議。原草圖把人體畫成要加汽油的車；你想保留食物供能的燃料意象，但改成吃食物的人物及簡單機器對照，避免小讀者當成真引擎。用一至兩句英文說明如何修改。

examples.en: Show food as the fuel that keeps the body running, but replace the petrol pump with a simple meal beside the active child. The engine shape should remain a comparison, not a literal picture of the body.
examples.zh: 把食物呈現為身體運作的燃料，但用活動孩子旁的簡單餐點取代油泵；引擎形狀應保持比喻，不是真人體圖。

examples.en: We can use the fuel that keeps the body running as the caption’s image for food energy. Please make the illustration show eating, rather than a child being filled with petrol.
examples.zh: 我們可在圖說用維持身體運作的燃料比喻食物能量；請圖中畫吃東西，不是向孩子加汽油。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以圖片及圖說的具體修改，保留能量對照又避免字面汽油；不把簡單圖像當精確營養說明。

takeaways.en: The traveller called the shared meal the fuel that kept the body running before another afternoon of carrying maps and cameras.
takeaways.zh: 旅人把共餐稱維持身體運作的燃料，準備下午繼續背地圖及相機。

takeaways.en: In the child’s story, food became the fuel that keeps the body running, just as the toy vehicle needed its own supply.
takeaways.zh: 孩子故事中，食物成為維持身體運作的燃料，就像玩具車也需自己的補給。
